clue.text: Vehicles carrying, say, those on a diet

indicators.note: vehicles carrying something hold it inside them, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as 'say' does

explanation.surface: Delivery trucks carrying slimmers somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Say is the usual crossword signal for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegans follow a strict plant-based eating regime, so they are people keeping to a particular diet.

clue.text: I've cleared no new in-person testimony

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the preceding letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: the twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A witness insists they have cleared nobody new while giving testimony.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral evidence is spoken by a witness in court, which is testimony given in person rather than in writing.

clue.text: Sheep eat oddly-laid flowers

indicators.note: animals that eat something take it inside, so these letters are swallowed by the other word
oddly points to the letters in odd positions of the following word

parts.note: first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: Rams munch on blooms someone has carelessly planted.
explanation.walkthrough: TUP is a northern British word for a ram; TUPS hold LI to give TULIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulips are spring-blooming bulb plants, an example of a kind of garden flower.

clue.text: Case of online tuition

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: found across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A legal case or instance of teaching delivered over the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental container for needles or cosmetics, a crossword favourite for a small case.

clue.text: Bit newspaper people in foot

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the final abbreviation

parts.note: a rag is a slang word for a poor newspaper

explanation.surface: A snippet of news about reporters getting into trouble on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag is a dismissive British word for a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a small broken-off piece, just as a bit is a small portion of something.

clue.text: Enemy workplace

parts.note: the single word is read as two, work and place
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A hostile office where colleagues are at war.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word workplace splits into work and place.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposition are those ranged against you in a contest or war, your adversaries or foe.

clue.text: Respond, replacing a terrible forward

indicators.note: replacing means one letter is swapped out of the first word for another piece

explanation.surface: A footballer answers back after a bad striker is replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: The A in REACT gives way to DIRE. Forward looks like a footballing noun but is the verb, as in forwarding mail.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a letter or email is to send it on to another address, which is to redirect it.

clue.text: Trade cut affected supplier of eye drops

indicators.note: letters that are affected are changed, so the fodder is rearranged

explanation.surface: A trade restriction hits a pharmaceutical firm making eye drops.
explanation.walkthrough: Eye drops sounds like a medicine from a supplier; here the drops are tears.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear duct produces and carries tears, the natural drops that fall from the eye.

clue.text: Free masks possibly included with obviously muscular physique

indicators.note: something included is put inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: personal protective equipment, of which masks are an example

explanation.surface: Someone muscular gets free masks thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: Masks are given only as an example of protective kit, hence 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripped is slang for having highly defined, visibly toned muscles from training.

clue.text: Anxious Australian wearing nothing is very cold

indicators.note: something wearing a garment is inside it, so the first letter sits within the next word

parts.note: a biting wind is very cold

explanation.surface: A nervous Aussie wearing no clothes is freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: Wearing is the container signal: the Australian goes inside nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nail-biting describes tense, nerve-racking suspense, from the habit of chewing fingernails when worried.

clue.text: Mixture of 50% recycled oil

indicators.note: fifty per cent means half of the word just before it is kept
recycled material is reprocessed, so these letters are reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A blend made partly from recycled cooking oil.
explanation.walkthrough: Of looks like a link word, but half of it supplies the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An olio is a spicy Spanish stew, and by extension any hotchpotch or miscellany.

clue.text: Awards no marks

parts.note: scars are marks on the skin

explanation.surface: Prizes given without any points scored.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscars are the Academy Awards, Hollywood's annual film prizes.

clue.text: Maybe flat road north is blocked by hundreds of teeth

indicators.note: a road blocked by something has that thing sitting in the middle of it

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's Great North Road, with 1 written as I
C is the Roman hundred, so two of them

explanation.surface: A flat tyre on a northbound road blocked by hundreds of sharp teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Flat suggests a tyre or apartment, but it is the musical sign; the A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: In music an accidental is a sharp, flat or natural sign added to a note, so a flat is one example.

clue.text: I need job, possibly as vice-president

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among several, so the letters may be reordered

explanation.surface: A jobseeker hopes to be picked as running mate.
explanation.definitionFit: He served as Barack Obama's deputy for two terms before becoming president, so vice-president is a former title of his.

clue.text: Physicist, one sparkling in interviews

indicators.note: interviews are spoken, so what matters is how the word is heard

parts.note: a gem is something that sparkles

explanation.surface: A brilliant scientist who shines when questioned by the press.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words are pronounced alike by many speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: James Prescott Joule was the English scientist after whom the unit of energy is named.

clue.text: Is breaking current record

indicators.note: breaking into something means entering it, so the first word goes inside

explanation.surface: An athlete is smashing the existing record.
explanation.walkthrough: Breaking and record suggest a sporting best, but record is a vinyl disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a flat vinyl disc carrying recorded sound.

clue.text: Persuade somehow, believing book is missing

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged in some other way
something missing is absent, so that letter is dropped from the word

explanation.surface: Coaxing someone into faith without scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop B from BELIEVING and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigle is to coax or cajole someone into doing something by flattery or trickery.

clue.text: Chase round area as ghosts do

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so the second word sits within the first

explanation.surface: Spectres pursuing someone around a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts are said to haunt the places they frequent, appearing there repeatedly after death.

clue.text: Golf's two followers limit what a player can have

parts.note: golf is G in the radio alphabet, and the two letters after G are H and I, read as H AND I

explanation.surface: Golfers are restricted in what they may carry on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf is the NATO code word for G.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer has a handicap, the number of strokes allowance reflecting ability, so it is something a player possesses.

clue.text: Odd characters in? I got that Greek one

indicators.note: odd characters are those in the first, third, fifth and seventh places of the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled by strange symbols claims to have understood the Greek one.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is one Greek character.

clue.text: See 2
Naughty Kelvin leaves a lot of washing-up

indicators.note: something that leaves goes away, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: as much dirty crockery as fills the basin
K is the symbol for the kelvin

explanation.surface: A naughty boy called Kelvin walks out on a pile of dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Kelvin looks like a name but is the unit of temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinful means wicked or wrong, and naughty is a milder word for misbehaving in that way.

clue.text: Heartless spy sat on space organisation

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter of each of the next two words goes

parts.note: an em is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A ruthless agent sat on a space agency.
explanation.walkthrough: Both spy and sat lose their middle letters; on places them over the final piece in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an orderly arrangement or method, which is what an organisation of parts provides.

clue.text: Channel's picture termed incomplete

indicators.note: incomplete words lose parts at both ends, so only a run inside them survives

parts.note: spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A television channel's film is described as unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: Channel suggests television; it is a tube in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The ureter is the duct carrying urine from kidney to bladder, an anatomical channel.

clue.text: Step down, not about to give autographs

indicators.note: not means the following word's letters are removed

parts.note: to step down is to quit a post

explanation.surface: A celebrity resigns but keeps signing for fans.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign is to write one's name, which is exactly what giving autographs involves.

clue.text: Sick sort of film director taking concessions back

indicators.note: taking something in holds it within, so one piece is placed inside another
back means the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: sops are small concessions to placate someone

explanation.surface: An arthouse director accepts favours in return and falls ill.
explanation.walkthrough: A sop is something offered to pacify, as in a sop to critics.
explanation.definitionFit: Indisposed is a polite word for slightly unwell, so it means sick.

clue.text: Swim across river, feeble one!

indicators.note: lying across something spans it, so the outer word wraps around the letter

explanation.surface: Taunting a weakling to swim to the other bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Drip is British slang for a dull, weak or spineless person, a wimp.

clue.text: Island off Australia has useless leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: An offshore island near Australia is said to be badly governed.
explanation.walkthrough: The island named is actually in the Pacific, nowhere near Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Oahu is the Hawaiian island that holds Honolulu and Pearl Harbor.

clue.text: Required from kleptomaniac, a plan to return high-end fabric

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the run is read right to left
required from means obtained out of these words, so the letters are inside them

explanation.surface: A thief plans to give back an expensive textile.
explanation.walkthrough: The fabric comes from a South American animal; high-end hints at the Andes, where they graze.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpaca is a soft luxurious wool woven from the fleece of a llama-like animal of the Andes.

clue.text: It's filled with melted cheese, as is Antarctica

indicators.note: a pie filled with something holds it inside, so the first word wraps the rest

parts.note: it is the subject that is filled

indicators.note: melted cheese loses its shape, so its letters are remoulded

explanation.surface: A toasted snack oozing with cheese, likened to the frozen continent.
explanation.walkthrough: It's reads as 'it is filled with', so the 's belongs to the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antarctica is covered by the world's largest continental ice mass, making it an example of this frozen formation.
